title: Allergy Action: Notice, Protect, Get Help

zones.label: Notice Signs
zones.summary: Possible allergy signs can affect skin, eyes, breathing, or digestion.
facts: Itchy eyes, hives, swelling, cough, wheeze, or stomach symptoms deserve attention.
Students should tell an adult rather than diagnose the cause themselves.
Symptoms can differ from one person or exposure to another.

zones.label: Stop Exposure
zones.summary: Move away from the possible allergen and do not eat or touch more.
facts: Set questionable food aside and avoid sharing it.
Leave an insect area safely after a sting.
Follow the person’s established allergy plan.

zones.label: Get an Adult
zones.summary: Tell a trusted, trained adult immediately about possible symptoms.
facts: Do not wait to see whether symptoms become severe.
Share what was eaten, touched, or noticed if known.
An adult can follow the individual care plan and contact family or professionals.

zones.label: Emergency Help
zones.summary: Trouble breathing or swelling of the face or throat needs emergency action now.
facts: Get trained adult and emergency help immediately.
Prescribed emergency medication should be used according to the person’s plan.
Never leave a person with severe symptoms alone.
